newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus central bank calls first Eurobond a success.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus central bank calls first Eurobond a success.

text.p: Officials at the Central Bank of Cyprus said on Friday the Republic's first long-term international bond issue was an unqualified sucess.
"The central bank is perfectly satisfied with the issue, especially with the fact that the issue was heavily oversubscribed," said Costas Poullis, manager at the central bank's foreign department.

The $300 million five-year bond was priced to yield 37 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, a high return for a single-A rated credit. The issue was over-subscribed even before it was launched on Thursday, officials at lead manager SBC Warburg said.
"Initially, the spread was 37 (basis points) but in the secondary market, we understand it is trading at around 36 points over treasury which is again, a positive development," Poullis told Reuters.
The bond was issued under a $500 million Euro medium-term note (EMTN) programme, recently established by Cyprus.
The proceeds will be used to refinance existing debt and fund development projects.

"For the time being, we do not expect any further public issues," said Poullis. "That will depend on the needs of the Republic of Cyprus, but we do not envisage any further issues...at least until the end of the year."
